messages:
anya: @channel Quick heads-up — we've landed a new compatibility policy and a docs checklist called 'DocShip' to reduce surprises during SDK releases. Short TL;DR: we now publish a 90-day 'compatibility corridor' for any minor SDK bumps, a mandatory migration guide template, and an optional deprecation telemetry opt-in. Please read the summary below and react if you need a follow-up.

mike: thank you! where's the checklist?

anya: https://redwood.internal/docs/docship-checklist (draft). key items: migration guide, example snippets, upgrade notes, QA prompt set, and a short rollback plan.

clare: +1 on the checklist. can we include an emergency rollback snippet for the hosted API? we've had a couple of incidents where customers needed it.

anya: yes — rollout plan explicitly requires a rollback section for hosted and dedicated. sample rollback commands are in the checklist.

sam: can you clarify "compatibility corridor"? is that like semver window or a calendar window?

anya: good Q. compatibility corridor = the supported semantic window we guarantee for client integration. e.g., a 0.x -> 0.y minor bump will be guaranteed to keep the same request/response contract for 90 days after release. after that, we can deprecate parts with a 30-day notice.

mike: and what about the private deployment package customers? we need to avoid breaking air-gapped installs.

anya: private customers get an extended corridor by default (180 days) and we will publish backported migration shims when feasible. we'll also notify Private account owners through account teams.

jordan: docs-bot: auto-generated checklist issue created: RFC-3197, PR #4821, migration-guide template attached.

docs-bot: PR link: https://git.redwood/rfcs/3197 , draft migration guide: https://git.redwood/infra/migration-templates/blob/main/sdk-migration.md

clare: who owns the migration guide for Python? I can volunteer but will need a small deck to sync with customer success.

anya: thanks Clare — please take Python. @mike can you cover JS compat snippets?

mike: happy to. I'll draft the snippet set and a small automation to run the QA prompt set against canary.

sam: automation sounds great. can we get an opt-in telemetry flag for deprecation events so we can measure real-world breakage?

anya: yes — the policy includes an opt-in telemetry hook for SDKs called compat_telemetry_enabled. it's opt-in and documented. we will only surface aggregate counts to product/eng.

jordan: product request: add a short banner in the console for affected customers during the corridor window.

anya: noted. I'll loop in Console PM to coordinate.

mike: timeline? when does this become policy?

anya: policy effective next Monday (90-day corridor starts from the first compatible minor release after that date). migration checklist and templates are usable immediately (draft). we'll lock PR after one week of feedback.

clare: ok adding to my calendar. can we schedule a 30-min sync with CS and PM tomorrow?

anya: yes — 10:30am PT tomorrow works for me. I'll send invite.

sam: tiny nit — can we avoid the word "deprecation" in public changelogs? it scares customers. maybe use "scheduled removal" + migration notes.

anya: good point. we'll standardize consumer-facing language in the migration guide template. internal docs can use the precise terms.

mike: :thumbsup:

docs-bot: Reminder set: review draft PR in 5 days.

anya: thanks all. if you plan to contribute, drop a quick note in the PR so we can assign reviewers. Appreciated!
